To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) semantic scene completion is a challenging task that can benefit from a deep learning framework; 2) a single depth image is sufficient for the task; 3) a 3D convolution network with dilation can learn the context of the scene and perform semantic scene completion; and 4) a dataset of synthetic 2D and 3D scenes is useful for training and evaluating such networks.
We introduce the semantic scene completeness problem, which aims to simultaneously predict the volumetric occupancy and the semantic labels of the 3D scene from a single depth image.
we propose a new method for semantic scene completion from a single depth image and we introduce a large-scale synthetic dataset for training.

the problem of estimating a 3D occupancy grid and its semantic segmentation from a single depth image.
the problem of semantic scene completion, i.e., producing a 3D voxelized occupancy and semantic labels from a single depth image.
